instruction: Implement `debounce(fn, wait)` in debounce.js (CommonJS, `module.exports = { debounce }`). The returned function delays calling `fn` until `wait` ms have passed since the last call, then calls it once with the latest arguments and `this`. It must have a `.cancel()` method that drops a pending call. Use the global `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` (looked up at call time).

Implement `throttle(fn, wait)` in throttle.js (`module.exports = { throttle }`). Leading and trailing edge: the first call runs `fn` immediately; further calls during the next `wait` ms are collapsed into ONE trailing call (with the latest args) that fires when the window ends; after a trailing call a new window of `wait` ms begins. If no extra call arrived, no trailing call happens. Add `.cancel()` to drop a pending trailing call and reset the window. Use global `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout` and `Date.now` looked up at call time.

Implement `debounce(fn, wait, options)` in debounce.js (`module.exports = { debounce }`). Options: `leading` (default false) and `trailing` (default true), plus `maxWait` (optional number). With `leading: true` the first call of a burst runs immediately; with `trailing: true` a call runs after `wait` ms of silence, but only if there was at least one call since the last invocation (so a single leading-only call does not fire twice). If `maxWait` is set, `fn` must be invoked (trailing) at latest `maxWait` ms after the first call of a burst even if calls keep arriving. Provide `.cancel()` and `.flush()` (runs a pending trailing call now and returns its result, otherwise returns undefined). Calls return the last result of `fn`. Use global `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout`/`Date.now` at call time.

Implement `formatDate(date, pattern)` in dates.js (`module.exports = { formatDate }`). `date` is a Date; use UTC getters. Pattern tokens: YYYY, YY, MMMM (January), MMM (Jan), MM, M, DD, D, HH (00-23), H, hh (01-12), h, mm, ss, A (AM/PM). Text inside square brackets is output literally, brackets removed, e.g. `[at] HH:mm`. Any other character is copied as is. Longer tokens win over shorter ones.

Implement `relativeTime(then, now)` in rel.js (`module.exports = { relativeTime }`); both arguments are epoch milliseconds. Return 'just now' if the absolute difference is under 60 seconds. Otherwise pick the largest unit among minute, hour, day (24h), month (30 days), year (365 days) whose floor value is >= 1, and return `'N unit(s) ago'` for the past or `'in N unit(s)'` for the future; use the singular for N = 1 ('1 hour ago', 'in 1 day').

Implement `formatCurrency(amount, opts)` in money.js (`module.exports = { formatCurrency }`) without Intl. Options: `symbol` (default '$'), `decimals` (default 2), `thousands` (default ','), `decimal` (default '.'). Round half away from zero to `decimals`, group the integer part in threes, and put the minus sign before the symbol: `-$1,234.50`. Never output '-$0.00' (a negative amount that rounds to zero is formatted as positive).

Implement `formatBytes(n, decimals = 1)` in bytes.js (`module.exports = { formatBytes }`): base 1024, units B, KB, MB, GB, TB. 0 -> '0 B'; values below 1024 print as integers with ' B'. Otherwise round to `decimals` places and drop trailing zeros ('1 KB', '1.5 KB'). Values >= 1024 TB stay in TB. Throw a RangeError for negative or non-finite input.

Implement `formatDuration(seconds)` in dur.js (`module.exports = { formatDuration }`). Floor to whole seconds. Under a minute: '45s'. Under an hour: '1m 05s' (seconds zero-padded). One hour or more: '1h 02m 03s' (minutes and seconds zero-padded). 0 -> '0s'. Negative input throws RangeError.

Implement `truncate(text, max)` in text.js (`module.exports = { truncate }`). If `text.length <= max` return it unchanged. Otherwise the result (including a final '…' character) must be at most `max` characters long. Prefer cutting at the last whitespace within the first `max - 1` characters (and trim trailing whitespace before adding '…'); if there is no whitespace to cut at (index 0 or none), hard-cut at `max - 1`.

Implement `slugify(s)` in slug.js (`module.exports = { slugify }`): lowercase, strip diacritics (NFD, remove combining marks), replace every run of non-alphanumeric ASCII characters with a single '-', and trim '-' from both ends. Non-strings are converted with String().

Implement `escapeHtml(v)` in esc.js (`module.exports = { escapeHtml }`): escape & < > " ' as & < > " '. null and undefined become ''. Other values are converted with String() first. Also export `html` as a tagged template function that escapes every interpolated value but not the literal parts: html`${name}`.

Implement `classNames(...args)` in cx.js (`module.exports = { classNames }`): returns a space-joined class string. Strings and numbers (non-zero) are included as is; falsy values are ignored; arrays are flattened recursively; objects include each key whose value is truthy. No dedupe, no extra spaces.

Implement `parseQuery(str)` and `buildQuery(obj)` in qs.js (`module.exports = { parseQuery, buildQuery }`). parseQuery accepts strings with or without a leading '?', splits on '&', decodes keys and values with decodeURIComponent after turning '+' into space, a key without '=' has value ''; repeated keys produce an array in order of appearance (a single occurrence stays a string); empty segments are skipped. buildQuery encodes with encodeURIComponent, skips null/undefined values, emits arrays as repeated keys, and returns the string without a leading '?'.

Implement `render(template, data)` in tpl.js (`module.exports = { render }`). `{{ path.to.value }}` (whitespace around the path allowed) inserts the value HTML-escaped (& < > " '); `{{{ path }}}` inserts it raw. Paths use dots and may index arrays (`items.0.name`). Missing/null/undefined values render as ''. Numbers and booleans are stringified (false -> 'false', 0 -> '0'). Everything else in the template is literal.

Implement `matchRoute(pattern, path)` in router.js (`module.exports = { matchRoute }`). Return an object of params or null. Patterns are segment based: literal segments must match exactly, `:name` captures one non-empty segment (value decoded with decodeURIComponent), and a final `*` captures the rest of the path (joined with '/') as params['*'] (may be empty string). A trailing slash on either side is ignored. Ignore any `?query` or `#hash` part of `path`. A match without params returns {}.

Implement `isEmail(s)` in email.js (`module.exports = { isEmail }`) for a sign-up form (not full RFC 5322). Valid: exactly one '@'; non-empty local part without spaces and not starting/ending with '.' and without '..'; domain made of at least two dot-separated labels, each 1-63 chars of letters, digits or hyphen, not starting/ending with hyphen; final label (TLD) letters only, 2+ chars. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed first. Non-strings are invalid.

Implement `passwordErrors(pw)` in pw.js (`module.exports = { passwordErrors }`). Return an array of error codes (empty array = valid) in this exact order: 'min8' (fewer than 8 chars), 'lower' (no a-z), 'upper' (no A-Z), 'digit' (no 0-9), 'symbol' (no character that is not a letter, digit or whitespace), 'space' (contains any whitespace). Non-strings return ['min8','lower','upper','digit','symbol'].

Implement `validateForm(values, rules)` in form.js (`module.exports = { validateForm }`). `rules` maps field name -> rule object with optional keys `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern` (RegExp), `min`, `max` (numbers), `custom` (function(value, allValues) returning an error string or null/undefined) and `messages` (object overriding default messages by rule name). String values are trimmed before checking. Rules run in the order required, minLength, maxLength, pattern, min, max, custom and the FIRST failing rule produces the field's error. Default messages: required 'Required', minLength 'Too short', maxLength 'Too long', pattern 'Invalid format', min 'Too small', max 'Too large'. A non-required field that is empty (after trim, or undefined/null) skips every other rule. min/max compare Number(value); a non-numeric value fails with 'Invalid number' (override key `number`). The `custom` message is whatever the function returns. Return `{ valid, errors }` where errors only has keys for failing fields and `valid` is true when there are none.

Implement `isValidCard(input)` in card.js (`module.exports = { isValidCard }`): strip spaces and hyphens, the remainder must be 12 to 19 digits and pass the Luhn checksum. Anything else (letters, other separators, non-strings) is false. Also export `cardBrand(input)` returning 'visa' (starts with 4), 'mastercard' (51-55 or 2221-2720), 'amex' (34 or 37) or 'unknown'.

Implement `formatPhone(input)` in phone.js (`module.exports = { formatPhone }`) for US numbers: keep only digits; an 11-digit number must start with '1' (dropped); after that exactly 10 digits are required, the area code and exchange must not start with 0 or 1; return `(555) 123-4567`, otherwise return null.

Implement `sortRows(rows, key, dir = 'asc')` in sort.js (`module.exports = { sortRows }`). Return a NEW array (do not mutate the input) sorted by `row[key]`. Numbers compare numerically; everything else compares as case-insensitive strings. If both values are numeric strings of the form '12' or '3.5' compare them numerically too. `null`/`undefined`/'' values always sort LAST, for both directions. The sort is stable (ties keep original order, also for 'desc'). `dir` is 'asc' or 'desc'; anything else throws a TypeError.

Implement `filterRows(rows, query, keys)` in filter.js (`module.exports = { filterRows }`). Split `query` on whitespace into terms. A row matches when EVERY positive term occurs (case-insensitive substring) in at least one of the stringified `row[key]` values for `keys`, and NO term that starts with '-' (and has more characters, e.g. '-draft') occurs in any of them. A lone '-' is an ordinary term. An empty/blank query returns a shallow copy of all rows. null/undefined values count as ''.

Implement `paginate(items, page, size)` in page.js (`module.exports = { paginate }`). Pages are 1-based; `page` is clamped into [1, pages] (and non-integers/NaN count as 1); `pages = max(1, ceil(total/size))`. Return `{ items, page, pages, total, start, end, hasPrev, hasNext }` where start/end are the 1-based position of the first/last item shown (both 0 when there are no items). `size < 1` or non-integer throws RangeError.

Implement `pageRange(current, total, max = 7)` in range.js (`module.exports = { pageRange }`) for a pagination control with at most `max` slots (max >= 5). Return an array of page numbers and the string '…' (ellipsis). If total <= max return 1..total. Otherwise the first and last page are always shown and the array always has exactly `max` entries: near the start (current <= max-3) `[1..max-2, '…', total]`; near the end (current >= total-max+4) `[1, '…', total-max+3..total]`; otherwise `[1, '…', <max-4 pages around current>, '…', total]` where the window starts at `current - floor((max-5)/2)`. Example for max 7, total 10: current 1..4 -> [1,2,3,4,5,'…',10]; current 5 -> [1,'…',4,5,6,'…',10]; current 7..10 -> [1,'…',6,7,8,9,10].

Implement `highlight(text, query)` in hl.js (`module.exports = { highlight }`) returning an HTML string safe to assign to innerHTML: the text is HTML-escaped (& < > " ') and every case-insensitive occurrence of `query` is wrapped in `<mark>...</mark>` (keeping the original casing). The query is literal text, not a regex (so '.' or '(' must work). Matches do not overlap. An empty query returns just the escaped text. A query containing '<' matches against the original text, not the escaped output.

Implement a pure tabs state machine in tabs.js (`module.exports = { initTabs, tabsReducer }`). `initTabs(count, {selected = 0, disabled = []})` returns `{count, selected, focused, disabled}` with focused = selected. `tabsReducer(state, action)` returns a NEW state (never mutate) or the SAME object when nothing changes. Actions: `{type:'key', key}` where key is 'ArrowRight' / 'ArrowLeft' (move focus to the next/previous ENABLED tab, wrapping around), 'Home' / 'End' (first / last enabled tab); automatic activation means `selected` follows `focused`. `{type:'select', index}` selects and focuses that tab unless it is out of range or disabled. Any other key returns the same state.

Implement an accordion state machine in accordion.js (`module.exports = { initAccordion, accordionReducer }`). `initAccordion({multiple = false, open = []})` returns `{multiple, open}` where open is an array of open panel ids (in single mode only the first given id is kept). `accordionReducer(state, action)` returns a NEW state without mutating the old one. Actions: `{type:'toggle', id}`: an open panel closes; a closed panel opens (in single mode all others close, in multiple mode it is appended). `{type:'expandAll', ids}` (only in multiple mode: open = all ids, keeping order; ignored in single mode), `{type:'collapseAll'}`. Unknown actions return the same state.

Implement `createModalStack()` in modals.js (`module.exports = { createModalStack }`) managing stacked dialogs. Methods: `open(id)` pushes id on top (if it is already open it is moved to the top, no duplicates), `close(id)` removes that id wherever it is (no-op if not open), `escape()` closes only the TOP modal and returns its id (or null if none), `top()` returns the top id or null, `isOpen(id)`, `ids()` returns a copy of the stack bottom->top, `scrollLocked()` is true while at least one modal is open. `onChange(fn)` registers a listener called with `{ids, scrollLocked}` after every call that actually changes the stack; it returns an unsubscribe function.

Implement `createToasts({max = 3})` in toasts.js (`module.exports = { createToasts }`). `add(message, {duration = 0} = {})` returns a numeric id (1, 2, 3, ... in call order), shows the toast if fewer than `max` are visible, otherwise queues it (FIFO). `visible()` returns copies of the visible toasts `{id, message}` in insertion order, `queued()` returns the queued count. `dismiss(id)` removes a visible or queued toast; when a visible one is removed the oldest queued toast becomes visible. If `duration > 0`, a toast auto-dismisses `duration` ms AFTER it becomes visible (queued toasts do not tick while queued). Use global `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout`. `dismiss` on an unknown id does nothing and returns false, otherwise true.

Implement `createWizard(steps, validators = {})` in wizard.js (`module.exports = { createWizard }`). `steps` is an array of step names. Methods: `state()` returns `{index, step, isFirst, isLast, reached}` (reached = highest index visited, starts at 0); `next(data)`: if a validator exists for the current step name it is called with `data` and must return true, otherwise `next` returns false and nothing changes; on the last step a successful `next` returns true without moving; otherwise it moves forward, updates `reached` and returns true. `back()` moves back one step (no-op on the first step, returns false then, otherwise true). `goTo(i)` jumps to index i only if 0 <= i <= reached (returns true/false).

Implement `createCarousel({count, loop = true, interval = 0})` in carousel.js (`module.exports = { createCarousel }`). Methods: `index()`, `next()`, `prev()`, `goTo(i)` (ignored if i is not an integer in range), `start()`, `stop()`, `running()`. With `loop` true next/prev wrap around; with loop false they stay at the ends. `start()` (only when interval > 0) calls `next()` every `interval` ms using global `setInterval`/`clearInterval`; any manual next/prev/goTo while running restarts the interval timer (so the next auto-advance is `interval` ms after the manual action). With `loop: false` autoplay stops itself after reaching the last slide. `start()` twice must not create a second timer. `stop()` clears the timer.

Implement `createHistory(initial, {limit = 100} = {})` in history.js (`module.exports = { createHistory }`), an undo/redo stack for an editor. Methods: `present()`, `push(value)` (makes value the present, clears the redo stack; ignored when `value === present()`), `undo()`, `redo()` (both return true if they moved, false otherwise), `canUndo()`, `canRedo()`. At most `limit` undo steps are kept (the oldest are dropped).

Implement `todoReducer(state = [], action)` and `visibleTodos(todos, filter)` in todos.js (`module.exports = { todoReducer, visibleTodos }`). A todo is `{id, text, done}`. Actions: `{type:'add', text}` (trim the text; blank text is ignored; id = max existing id + 1, or 1), `{type:'toggle', id}`, `{type:'remove', id}`, `{type:'edit', id, text}` (trimmed; blank text removes the todo), `{type:'clearCompleted'}`, `{type:'toggleAll'}` (if every todo is done mark all not done, otherwise mark all done). Never mutate the old state; todos that did not change keep the same object identity; an action that changes nothing returns the same array. `visibleTodos(todos, 'all' | 'active' | 'done')` filters; unknown filter returns all.

Implement `createStore(reducer, initialState)` in store.js (`module.exports = { createStore }`), a minimal Redux-like store. `getState()`, `dispatch(action)` (calls reducer(state, action), stores the result, then notifies listeners with no arguments, and returns the action; throws if the action is not an object with a string `type`), `subscribe(listener)` returns an unsubscribe function (idempotent). Listeners are notified from a snapshot taken when notification starts: a listener added during notification is NOT called until the next dispatch, and the snapshot is used as-is (so a listener unsubscribed by an earlier listener in the same round is still called that round). Subscribing the same function twice makes two registrations; each unsubscribe removes only its own. Calling `dispatch` from inside the reducer must throw an Error('Reducers may not dispatch'). The reducer is NOT called at creation time.

Implement `createEmitter()` in emitter.js (`module.exports = { createEmitter }`) with `on(event, fn)` (returns an unsubscribe function), `once(event, fn)` (also returns unsubscribe; the handler runs at most once), `off(event, fn)` (removes ONE registration of fn; no-op if absent), `emit(event, ...args)` which calls handlers in registration order with args and returns the number of handlers called, and `listenerCount(event)`. emit iterates a snapshot: handlers added during an emit run only on later emits, and handlers removed during an emit (including a `once` handler removing itself) must not break the iteration of the others.

Implement `nextIndex(current, key, len, opts)` in nav.js (`module.exports = { nextIndex }`) for keyboard navigation of a listbox/menu. `current` is the active index or -1 for none. Keys: ArrowDown (+1), ArrowUp (-1), Home (first enabled), End (last enabled), PageDown (+10), PageUp (-10); any other key returns `current` unchanged. `opts = {wrap = true, disabled = []}`. With wrap, ArrowDown/ArrowUp wrap around the ends; PageUp/PageDown never wrap, they clamp to the first/last enabled item. Disabled indices are skipped (a stepping key moves to the next enabled one in that direction). From -1 ArrowDown goes to the first enabled item and ArrowUp to the last enabled one. If `len` is 0 or every item is disabled, return -1. Without wrap, stepping beyond the ends returns `current`.

Implement `visibleRange({scrollTop, viewportHeight, itemHeight, total, overscan = 3})` in virtual.js (`module.exports = { visibleRange }`) for a virtualised list. Return `{start, end, offsetTop, totalHeight}` where `start` (inclusive) = max(0, floor(scrollTop/itemHeight) - overscan), `end` (exclusive) = min(total, ceil((scrollTop+viewportHeight)/itemHeight) + overscan), `offsetTop = start*itemHeight`, `totalHeight = total*itemHeight`. Negative scrollTop counts as 0. total 0 gives start 0, end 0. `itemHeight <= 0` throws RangeError.

Implement `starFill(rating, max = 5)` in stars.js (`module.exports = { starFill }`) returning an array of `max` strings 'full' | 'half' | 'empty' for a star-rating display. The rating is first clamped to [0, max] and rounded to the nearest 0.5 (halves round up: 3.25 -> 3.5, 3.75 -> 4); NaN counts as 0. Example: starFill(3.5) -> ['full','full','full','half','empty'].

Implement `computePosition(anchor, tip, viewport, opts)` in pos.js (`module.exports = { computePosition }`) for a tooltip/popover. `anchor = {x, y, width, height}`, `tip = {width, height}`, `viewport = {width, height}`, `opts = {placement = 'top', gap = 8, margin = 4}`. Placement 'top'/'bottom' centre the tip horizontally on the anchor and put it above (y = anchor.y - tip.height - gap) / below (y = anchor.y + anchor.height + gap); 'left'/'right' centre it vertically and put it left (x = anchor.x - tip.width - gap) / right (x = anchor.x + anchor.width + gap). If the preferred side does not fit inside the viewport (respecting `margin` on that side) but the opposite side does, flip to the opposite side; if neither fits keep the preferred one. After placing, clamp the position so the tip stays within [margin, viewport - size - margin] on both axes (if the tip is larger than the space, the min bound wins). Return `{x, y, placement}` where placement is the final side.

Implement `assignColumns(heights, n)` in masonry.js (`module.exports = { assignColumns }`). Distribute items (given by their heights, in order) into `n` columns, always putting the next item into the currently shortest column; ties go to the lowest column index. Return `{columns, totals}` where columns is an array of n arrays of item indices and totals the summed height per column. n < 1 or non-integer throws RangeError.

Implement `getMonthGrid(year, month, weekStart = 0)` in cal.js (`module.exports = { getMonthGrid }`) for a calendar widget. `month` is 0-11, `weekStart` 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday. Return an array of weeks; each week is 7 cells `{date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', day: <number>, inMonth: <boolean>}`. The grid starts on the first `weekStart` day on or before the 1st of the month and ends on the last day-of-week before the next week start after the last of the month, so it contains only as many weeks as needed (4 to 6). Leading/trailing cells are the neighbouring months' days with inMonth false. Use UTC arithmetic only (no local time).

Implement UTC date helpers in dateutil.js (`module.exports = { addDays, isSameDay, daysBetween, startOfWeek, isWeekend }`). All use UTC fields. `addDays(date, n)` returns a NEW Date n days later (n may be negative or large; the input is not mutated). `isSameDay(a, b)` compares UTC year/month/day. `daysBetween(a, b)` = number of whole calendar days from a to b (UTC dates, ignoring time of day; negative if b is earlier). `startOfWeek(date, weekStart = 0)` returns a new Date at 00:00:00.000 UTC of the most recent weekStart day (0 = Sunday) on or before date. `isWeekend(date)` is true for Saturday and Sunday.

Implement WCAG colour contrast helpers in contrast.js (`module.exports = { contrastRatio, passesAA }`). `contrastRatio(fg, bg)` takes hex colours '#rgb' or '#rrggbb' (with or without '#', any case) and returns the WCAG 2.x ratio (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) with L1 the lighter relative luminance; sRGB channels are linearised with c <= 0.03928 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4. `passesAA(fg, bg, {large = false})` is true when the ratio is >= 4.5 (>= 3 for large text). Invalid colour strings throw a TypeError.

Implement colour helpers in color.js (`module.exports = { hexToRgb, rgbToHex, lighten }`). `hexToRgb('#abc' | 'aabbcc' | '#AABBCC')` returns `[r, g, b]`; invalid input returns null. `rgbToHex(r, g, b)` rounds and clamps each channel to 0..255 and returns lowercase '#rrggbb'. `lighten(hex, amount)` mixes the colour towards white by `amount` (0..1, clamped): channel = round(c + (255 - c) * amount); returns '#rrggbb' lowercase, null for invalid hex.

Implement `rankSuggestions(items, query, limit = 5)` in suggest.js (`module.exports = { rankSuggestions }`). `items` are strings. Return up to `limit` items matching `query` (trimmed, case-insensitive substring), ordered by score: 0 exact match, 1 starts with the query, 2 a word inside starts with the query (word = after a space, '-' or '_'), 3 contains it elsewhere; ties are broken by shorter length, then alphabetically (case-insensitive, then original). Duplicates (case-insensitive) are listed once (keep the first). A blank query returns [].

Implement `diffValues(initial, current)` in dirty.js (`module.exports = { diffValues }`) for form dirty tracking. Return `{changed, dirty}` where `changed` is the alphabetically sorted list of keys (from either object) whose values differ and `dirty` is `changed.length > 0`. Primitives compare with ===; arrays compare element-wise with ===; a key missing on one side counts as different from any value on the other side (including undefined only if the key is missing - a present key with value undefined equals a missing key).

Implement `createStorage(store, prefix = '')` in storage.js (`module.exports = { createStorage }`), a safe JSON wrapper around a Web-Storage-like object (`getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`, and `length`/`key(i)` for enumeration). Methods: `get(key, fallback = null)` returns the parsed JSON value, or `fallback` when the key is missing, the stored text is invalid JSON, or the store throws; `set(key, value)` stores JSON and returns true, or returns false if the store throws (quota/private mode) or the value cannot be serialised (circular, undefined); `remove(key)` never throws; `keys()` returns the un-prefixed keys that start with the prefix (in store order). Real keys are `prefix + key`.

Implement `matchesMedia(query, width)` in mq.js (`module.exports = { matchesMedia }`), a tiny evaluator for media queries against a viewport width in px. Supported: `(min-width: Npx)`, `(max-width: Npx)` (inclusive comparisons), conditions joined with `and`, alternatives joined with a comma (OR), an optional leading `screen` or `all` media type, case-insensitive, flexible whitespace. Any query containing a feature or media type it does not understand (e.g. `print`, `(orientation: portrait)`) is false (for that comma alternative). An empty query is true. Also support `min-width`/`max-width` values in `em` (1em = 16px).

Implement `moveItem(list, from, to)` in reorder.js (`module.exports = { moveItem }`) for drag-and-drop / keyboard reordering. Return a NEW array with the element at index `from` removed and inserted so that it ends up at index `to` of the result. Out-of-range or non-integer `from` returns an unchanged copy; `to` is clamped to [0, length-1]. Never mutate the input.

Implement `compactNumber(n)` in compact.js (`module.exports = { compactNumber }`) for counters ('1.2K views'). |n| < 1000 prints as is (rounded to an integer). Otherwise scale by 1000 steps with suffixes K, M, B, T and show at most one decimal, dropping '.0' ('1K', '1.2K', '15K', '999.9K'). Rounding that reaches 1000 in the current unit must promote to the next unit (999999 -> '1M', 999950 -> '1M', 999949 -> '999.9K'). Keep the sign ('-1.5K'). Above 999.9T keep T (e.g. '1500T'). Non-finite input returns '0'.

Implement `pluralize(count, singular, plural)` in plural.js (`module.exports = { pluralize }`) returning e.g. '1 item', '0 items', '2 items', '1,234 items'. If `plural` is omitted use `singular + 's'`; when singular ends in 's', 'x', 'z', 'ch' or 'sh' add 'es'; when it ends in a consonant + 'y' change to 'ies'. Absolute value 1 is singular (so -1 -> '-1 item'); 1.0 too; 1.5 -> '1.5 items'. Integers are grouped with thousands commas.

Implement `memoizeLast(fn)` in memo.js (`module.exports = { memoizeLast }`): returns a function that caches only the most recent call. If called again with the same number of arguments and every argument `===` the previous one (and the same `this`), return the cached result without calling `fn`; otherwise call `fn` and cache. If `fn` throws, nothing is cached. The wrapper has a `.clear()` method.

Implement `initTabs(root)` in tabs.js (`module.exports = { initTabs }`) that makes this markup an accessible tab widget: `root` contains one `.tablist` element holding `.tab` buttons and, in the same order, `.panel` elements. Set `role=tablist` on the list, `role=tab` on tabs, `role=tabpanel` on panels; give every tab and panel an id if it lacks one (e.g. `${root.id || 'tabs'}-tab-0`), link them with `aria-controls` (tab -> panel) and `aria-labelledby` (panel -> tab). from checklib import *
css = Css(open('style.css').read())
import re

def ncols(v):
    if not v: return 0
    m = re.match(r'repeat\((\d+),', v)
    if m: return int(m.group(1))
    return len([t for t in re.split(r'\s+(?![^()]*\))', v.strip()) if t])
def num(v):
    m = re.match(r'(-?[0-9.]+)', v or '')
    return float(m.group(1)) if m else None

fs = css.get('.prose', 'font-size') or ''
v = num(fs)
ok(v is not None and ((fs.endswith('rem') or fs.endswith('em')) and v >= 1 or fs.endswith('px') and v >= 16), 'font-size >= 16px: %r' % fs)
lh = css.get('.prose', 'line-height') or ''
ok(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9.]+', lh) is not None and 1.4 <= float(lh) <= 1.8, 'unitless line-height 1.4-1.8: %r' % lh)
mw = css.get('.prose', 'max-width') or ''
ok(mw.endswith('ch') and 55 <= num(mw) <= 75, 'max-width 55-75ch: %r' % mw)
ok(css.get('.prose a', 'text-decoration') == 'underline' or (css.get('.prose a', 'text-decoration-line') == 'underline'), 'links underlined')
ok((css.get('.prose p+p', 'margin-top') or '').endswith('em') and num(css.get('.prose p+p', 'margin-top')) >= 0.75, 'paragraph spacing in em')
ok(css.get('.prose', 'color') == '#1f2937', 'colour kept')
finish()
